citation: Raz O, Steinvil A, Berliner S et al. (2013). The effect of two iso-caloric meals containing equal amounts of fats with a different fat composition on the inflammatory and metabolic markers in apparently healthy volunteers. Journal of Inflammation (London, England) 10:3-3.
protocol: Two iso-caloric breakfasts (~1160 kcal, ~56-57% fat), crossover 3 weeks apart: SFA meal (chicken sausages, fried potatoes, ketchup, mayonnaise; 24 g SFA, 33 g MUFA, 17 g PUFA) vs MUFA meal (pasta, olive oil, ketchup, nuts; 8 g SFA, 51 g MUFA, 14 g PUFA); fat scaled to body surface area. Blood at 0, 2, 4 h.
population: n=54 apparently healthy volunteers (38 women, 16 men), age 41.7 ± 3.1 y, BMI 25.9 ± 0.9 kg/m2.

reports.where: Table 3: 0, 2, 4 h by meal and sex, µU/mL

note: Paired-meal contrast, fat_type: saturated-rich sausage meal vs olive-oil pasta meal at matched energy and fat. One of few fat-type papers with insulin and glucose by time in a table. Watch: carbohydrate and protein grams are not printed and the foods differ a lot (only fat and energy are stated as matched), values split by sex (no pooled row), and the BMI "± 0.9" looks like an SEM.
